summary: Unexpected elevation in server errors for streaming-heavy route resulting in upstream runtime restarts
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightQuery reported a sudden, sustained rise in 5xx responses for long-lived streaming requests to the /v1/chat/stream endpoint starting ~2026-03-14T01:12:00Z. The increase correlates with a set of long-running half-closed streaming sessions and a large embedding upload that occurred from the same tenant.

Impact:
- Multiple BrightQuery production endpoints returned 502/503/504 for ~18 minutes, elevated error-rate observed across their region.
- Affected: small set of streaming and short-poll routes; overall tenant throughput degraded ~40% during window.
- Customer-facing SLAs potentially impacted; they contacted Support at 01:20 UTC.

Environment:
- Prod cluster: serving shard us-east-1-a (edge proxy pool ep-proxy-7..10)
- Runtime version: r-infer-2026-02-3b
- API gateway: front-door v2.4.1 (HTTP/2 multiplexing enabled)

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Customer opened several long-lived streaming sessions (idle for >120s with half-closed client socket).
2) Simultaneously performed a multithreaded embedding upload job that generated many short-lived connections to /v1/embeddings/bulk.
3) Edge logs show steady growth of accept-queue length on ep-proxy-9 and increased SYN_RECV counts.
4) Runtimes serving that tenant started showing repeated watchdog-triggered restarts and SIGABRT in runtime logs.

Observed metrics & logs (high-level):
- API gateway 5xx rate (tenant=brightquery): baseline 0.2% -> peak 18% (01:12-01:30 UTC).
- ep-proxy-9 accept_queue depth: 5 -> 512 within ~6 minutes (alerts fired).
- runtime (r-infer-2026-02-3b) worker OOM and watchdog_restart_count: 0 -> 7 on affected shard.
- dmesg excerpt (runtime): "oom_killer: kill process 23456 (r-infer) score 1956" and repeated "watchdog: GPU timeout, resetting context"
- api-gateway logs: a pattern of half-closed stream entries followed by immediate RST or 502 back to client.

Initial hypotheses considered:
- Accept-queue head-of-line blocking caused by many half-closed streams preventing new connections from being serviced.
- Ephemeral proxy connection slab exhaustion amplified by simultaneous embedding upload fanout.
- A runtime prefetch/caching codepath deadlock under mixed streaming+embedding workload causing memory pressure and GPU watchdog resets.

Investigation notes (chronological):
- 01:22 UTC: Support triaged; enabled tenant-level emergency rate cap at edge (temporary mitigation) — immediate drop in new connections from the tenant.
- 01:24 UTC: SRE restarted ep-proxy-9 and rotated accept queue settings; accept queue depths returned to normal.
- 01:27 UTC: Runtime restarts reduced after proxy restart and emergency cap; however three runtime instances required manual restart due to residual GPU context errors.
- 01:40 UTC: Confirmed embedding upload from BrightQuery had ~20 concurrent workers peaking at 200 RPS to embeddings endpoint. Correlation strong.

Workaround applied:
- Tenant emergency rate cap applied (ingress) to limit concurrent connections to streaming and embeddings endpoints.
- Restarted affected runtime replicas and ep-proxy pods to reclaim accept-queue slots.
- Customer advised to stagger embedding upload concurrency and to close idle streams promptly.

Root-cause (current working theory):
A combined ingress-level resource exhaustion (accept-queue/thread-slot saturation) from many short-lived embedding upload connections plus a set of long-lived half-closed streaming sessions created head-of-line blocking at the proxy layer. This prevented the proxy from handing off new ephemeral connections to runtimes, producing connection queuing and bursty retries that increased memory/GPU pressure on a small set of runtime replicas. Under that pressure a prefetch/cache race in runtime triggered GPU watchdog timeouts and process restarts, magnifying the 5xx surface for the tenant.

Immediate next steps:
- Engineering (SRE + Runtime) to review runtime prefetch/cancellation paths for streaming+bulk-embedding mixed workloads (ownership: @runtime-team).
- Adjust default proxy accept-queue timeout to proactively reject half-closed streams older than 60s (ownership: @edge-team).
- Create a tenant-concurrency advisory doc for customers performing large embedding uploads.
- Add a short-term detection rule to Alerting: "tenant accept-queue growth + high half-closed socket ratio".

Links / references:
- Grafana: https://grafana.internal.redwood/shot/brightquery-errors-2026-03-14
- Edge logs (ep-proxy-9): https://logs.internal/ep-proxy-9/2026-03-14
- Runtime logs (shard us-east-1-a): https://logs.internal/runtime/shard-us-east-1-a/2026-03-14
- Slack: #support (thread ts 1613456789.000200)

Desired outcome:
- Root cause confirmed and fix shipped to prevent combination of half-closed streaming + bursty embedding uploads from driving upstream runtime restarts and elevated 5xx.
- Customer BrightQuery receives post-incident summary and recommendations for safer upload patterns (staggered concurrency, stream keepalive pruning).
comments: 2026-03-14 01:21 UTC — Maya Chen (Support): Received initial report from BrightQuery. They reported 502/503 on production streams. Gathering logs and escalated to SRE.

2026-03-14 01:25 UTC — Lucas Peña (SRE): Applied tenant emergency ingress cap (limit=30 concurrent connections) and restarted ep-proxy-9. Initial error rate dropped. Captured accept-queue histograms and dmesg from runtime.

2026-03-14 01:33 UTC — Ana Rodríguez (Runtime eng): Observed repeated GPU watchdog resets in runtime logs; collecting core dumps. Suspect prefetch cancellation race under memory pressure. Investigating commit range around r-infer-2026-02-3b.
2026-03-14 02:10 UTC — Lucas Peña (SRE): Manual restarts completed for three affected runtime replicas. No further restarts after 02:05 UTC. Kept emergency cap while we validate fix route.

2026-03-14 09:00 UTC — Customer (BrightQuery contact: Priya Nair): Confirmed service recovered and they accepted temporary guidance to throttle upload concurrency for today's batch run. Asked for a post-incident write-up and timeline.

2026-03-15 10:12 UTC — Runtime eng (Ana Rodríguez): Reproduced tight reproduction in staging with a 1:5 ratio of half-closed streaming sessions to concurrent embedding uploads; created a minimal test harness. Patch created to cancel prefetch more aggressively under memory pressure. PR referenced below.
2026-03-16 16:40 UTC — Edge-team (Jun Park): Implemented provisional accept-queue timeout config change and rollout to us-east. Monitoring for regressions.
resolution: Mitigation in place: tenant rate cap and proxy accept-queue tuning. Runtime patch proposed to improve prefetch cancellation under pressure (PR 4821). Follow-ups scheduled: runtime patch merge + canary, permanent edge config change, customer advisory.
